info.title: coss.com API
info.description: One API key for every coss.com product. Errors share one envelope: `Error`. Every request is scoped to the environment the key belongs to; domains and the audit log are organization-wide.

tags.name: Environment
tags.description: The environment, project and organization an API key belongs to.

tags.name: Emails
tags.description: Send transactional email and follow its delivery.

tags.name: Email templates
tags.description: Versioned, localized subjects and bodies with typed variables, sent by id or alias.

tags.name: Suppressions
tags.description: Addresses that sends skip, added by bounces, complaints or you.

tags.name: Tracking
tags.description: Which emails of the environment have their opens and clicks tracked.

tags.name: SMS
tags.description: Send text messages from the organization's numbers, follow their delivery, and read replies and opt-outs.

tags.name: Dedicated IPs
tags.description: The organization's own sending IPs, warmed up automatically (an add-on).

tags.name: Webhook endpoints
tags.description: URLs that receive the environment's delivery events, signed.

tags.name: Hooks applications
tags.description: Hooks (webhooks as a service): your customers, each with their own endpoints and portal.

tags.name: Hooks event types
tags.description: The catalog of messages you send, which your customers subscribe from.

tags.name: Hooks endpoints
tags.description: Your customers' URLs that receive their messages, each signed with its own secret.

tags.name: Hooks messages
tags.description: Send a message once; coss.com delivers it to every subscribed endpoint, with retries.

tags.name: Hooks portal
tags.description: A ready-made page for your customers to manage their endpoints.

tags.name: Logs
tags.description: The environment's API requests, email events and webhook attempts.

tags.name: Audit log
tags.description: Changes to the organization, by members, API keys and coss.com support.

tags.name: Risk
tags.description: Assess sign-ups, logins and other events: a decision with reasons, from signals and what the environment remembers.

bearerAuth.description: A secret API key from the dashboard: `coss_live_…` for production environments, `coss_test_…` for sandbox environments.

slug.description: The project's slug, as in dashboard URLs.
The organization's slug, as in dashboard URLs.

api_version.description: The organization's pinned API version: what requests without a `Coss-Version` header and new webhook endpoints get.

start.description: The key's first characters, as shown in the dashboard.

access.description: `full`: every permission, including ones new products add later. `restricted`: only `permissions`, chosen when the key was created.

permissions.description: What the key may do now, as `resource:action` (the names `insufficient_permissions` errors use), e.g. `email:send`.

api_key.description: The API key making this request.

Environment.description: The environment an API key belongs to, with its project and organization.

param.description: The request field or header the error relates to.

issues.description: Every problem: of the request (`validation_error`) or of a template (`invalid_template_variables`, `template_invalid`).

status.description: Whether the email was handed to the delivery provider. `scheduled` emails wait for `scheduled_at`; `canceled` ones were canceled before that. Per-recipient delivery is in `recipients`.

failure.description: Why the email failed; `null` unless `status` is `failed`.

attachments.description: Attachment metadata. Content is never returned, and is discarded once sent.

sandbox.description: True when sent from a sandbox environment (never delivered).

scheduled_at.description: When the email was scheduled to be sent; `null` if it was not.

batch_id.description: The batch that sent the email; `null` if it was sent on its own.

template.description: The template the email was rendered from; `null` if it was sent without one.

broadcast_id.description: The broadcast the email is part of; `null` for any other email.

code.description: Why the email failed, e.g. `all_recipients_suppressed`, `domain_not_verified`, `content_rejected`, `attachments_unavailable`, `dispatch_failed` or `provider_error`.

examples.message: Every recipient is on the suppression list or unsubscribed.

status.description: Delivery status of this recipient. `suppressed` means the address is on the environment's suppression list (for every email or for this email's category), so it was skipped. `canceled` means the scheduled email was canceled before it was sent.

opens.description: Whether opens are tracked for this email.

clicks.description: Whether link clicks are tracked for this email.

unsubscribe.description: Whether the email carries one-click unsubscribe headers (RFC 8058).

EmailTracking.description: Open and click tracking, as resolved when the email was sent, with engagement so far. Opens can be inflated by mail clients that prefetch images, clicks by link scanners.

version.description: `null` for a dashboard test send of the draft.

mode.description: The environment's content storage when the email was sent. With `discard`, the subject, `html`, `text`, `headers`, template variables and attachment filenames are cleared once the email is sent, fails or is canceled.

discarded_at.description: When the content was cleared; `null` while it is kept. A cleared email has an empty `subject`, `html` and `text` `null` and no `headers`.

EmailContentStorage.description: Whether coss.com keeps the email's content after sending it.

from.description: An email address, optionally with a display name: "Acme <hello@acme.com>".

anyOf.description: An email address, optionally with a display name: "Acme <hello@acme.com>".

items.description: An email address, optionally with a display name: "Acme <hello@acme.com>".

items.description: An email address, optionally with a display name: "Acme <hello@acme.com>".

subject.description: Required unless the email is sent from a template (`template_id`).

text.description: Plain-text body. Without it, an `html` email goes out with a text part generated from the HTML.

template_id.description: Send a published email template (its id or alias) instead of `subject`, `html` and `text`.

template_version.description: A published version of the template to send. Defaults to the latest one.

locale.description: The template locale to send, e.g. "pt-BR". Falls back to the language ("pt"), then to the template's default locale.

variables.description: Values for the template's variables, keyed by name.

headers.description: Up to 15 custom headers. Names are case-insensitive.

category.description: What kind of email this is, e.g. "marketing". Recipients suppressed for this category (or for every email) are skipped.

scheduled_at.description: Send the email at this time instead of now (ISO 8601 with an offset, at most 30 days ahead). A time that is not in the future sends immediately. Scheduled emails can be rescheduled or canceled until they are sent.

attachments.description: Up to 20 files, at most 25 MB combined.

stream.description: `transactional` (the default) or `marketing`. Marketing email goes out on its own sending infrastructure and reputation, so its complaints never hold up transactional mail. It needs the environment's postal address (marketing settings), exactly one recipient, and no `List-Unsubscribe` header: coss.com adds one-click unsubscribe headers and a footer with the address and an unsubscribe link (place them yourself with `{{{unsubscribe_url}}}`, `{{{preferences_url}}}` and `{{{mailing_address}}}`). Contacts who unsubscribed are skipped.

content_id.description: Makes the attachment inline: reference it from `html` as ``.

opens.description: Add an invisible pixel to the HTML body and record `email.opened` events.

clicks.description: Send HTML links through a coss.com redirect and record `email.clicked` events. Links with a `data-coss-no-track` attribute are left alone.

unsubscribe.description: Add one-click unsubscribe headers (`List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post`, RFC 8058). An unsubscribe suppresses the recipient for this email's category and records `email.unsubscribed`. Needs a `category`, a single recipient, no `List-Unsubscribe` header of your own and at most 13 custom headers.

TrackingOptions.description: Overrides the environment's tracking settings (its default, or the rule for this email's category) for this email. Omitted fields keep the configured setting.

data.description: The batch's emails, in the order of the request.

emails.description: Up to 100 emails, each accepted by `POST /v1/emails`. The batch is accepted or rejected as a whole.

status.description: Whether the email was handed to the delivery provider. `scheduled` emails wait for `scheduled_at`; `canceled` ones were canceled before that. Per-recipient delivery is in `recipients`.

failure.description: Why the email failed; `null` unless `status` is `failed`.

sandbox.description: True when sent from a sandbox environment (never delivered).

scheduled_at.description: When the email was scheduled to be sent; `null` if it was not.

batch_id.description: The batch that sent the email; `null` if it was sent on its own.

template.description: The template the email was rendered from; `null` if it was sent without one.

broadcast_id.description: The broadcast the email is part of; `null` for any other email.

EmailSummary.description: An email without its content. Retrieve the email for `html`, `text`, `headers` and `attachments`.

scheduled_at.description: The new time to send the email at (ISO 8601 with an offset, at most 30 days ahead). A time that is not in the future sends it right away.

recipient.description: The recipient this event is about; `null` for the whole email.

reason.description: `bounce`: added after a permanent bounce. `complaint`: added after a spam complaint. `manual`: added one by one through the API or dashboard. `import`: added by a bulk import. `unsubscribe`: added by the recipient's one-click unsubscribe, scoped to the email's category.

suppression.description: Only for `email.suppressed`: the entry that matched the recipient.

unsubscribe.description: Only for `email.suppressed` without `suppression`: the recipient is a contact who unsubscribed (from marketing, or from the email's topic, `topic`).

url.description: The original link that was clicked.

link_position.description: Index of the link among the email's tracked links.

position.description: Index of the link among the tracked links.

published_version.description: The version sends use; `null` until the draft is first published.

has_unpublished_changes.description: Whether the draft was changed since it was last published.

alias.description: A name to send the template by instead of its id, e.g. `welcome`: the same alias can be used in every environment.

default_locale.description: The locale sends fall back to when they ask for none, or for one without content. Defaults to the first entry of `contents` (or "en").

variables.description: The variables the template uses, with their types.

sample_variables.description: Example values for previews and test sends in the dashboard.

contents.description: The subject, HTML and text per locale.

CreateEmailTemplateRequest.description: Creates the template and its draft. Publish the draft to send it.

type.description: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, or `list` (an array of objects with the declared `fields`, looped over with `{{#each name}}`).

required.description: Sends must pass it unless it has a `default`. Defaults to true.

default.description: Used when a send leaves it out. Not for lists.

fields.description: A list's item fields (required for lists, only for lists).

locale.description: A BCP 47 language tag, e.g. "en" or "pt-BR".

html.description: The HTML template. Provide `html`, `text`, or both.

anyOf.description: A name to send the template by instead of its id, e.g. `welcome`: the same alias can be used in every environment.

UpdateEmailTemplateRequest.description: Changes the template's name, alias or description. Content changes go to the draft.

version.description: The version number; `null` for the draft.

revision.description: Counts the draft's saves. A published version keeps the revision it was published from.

problems.description: Syntax errors and undeclared variables per locale and field, which keep a draft from being published. Always empty for published versions.

revision.description: The draft `revision` you read. When given, the request is refused (`template_revision_mismatch`) if the draft changed since.

default_locale.description: The locale sends fall back to when they ask for none, or for one without content. Defaults to the first entry of `contents` (or "en").

variables.description: The variables the template uses, with their types.

sample_variables.description: Example values for previews and test sends in the dashboard.

contents.description: The subject, HTML and text per locale.

UpdateEmailTemplateDraftRequest.description: Replaces the whole draft: fields left out are emptied (`default_locale` falls back to the first locale).

revision.description: The draft `revision` you read. When given, the request is refused (`template_revision_mismatch`) if the draft changed since.

version.description: The version rendered; `null` for the draft.
A published version to render. Default: the draft.

locale.description: The locale to render, e.g. "pt-BR". Falls back to the language ("pt"), then to the default locale, as sends do.

variables.description: Values by variable name, checked as a send checks them. Default: `sample_variables`.

RenderEmailTemplateRequest.description: What to render: nothing is sent or stored.

status.description: `pending` while the records are being checked, `verified` once they are, `temporary_failure` after a transient DNS problem, and `failed` when verification gave up (72 hours) — restart it with the verify endpoint. `deleting` is a removal in progress.

can_send.description: Whether live keys may send from this domain right now.

mail_from_domain.description: The envelope sender subdomain bounces come back to.

records.description: The DNS records to publish, with the result of the last check.

purpose.description: What the record is for: `dkim` signs messages, `mail_from_mx` and `mail_from_spf` set up the bounce subdomain, `dmarc` is recommended but not required.

name.description: The fully qualified record name to create.

required.description: `false` for records that are only recommended.

status.description: What the last DNS check saw. `not_checked` means DNS has not been consulted yet.

found.description: What DNS returned when it did not match.

hostname.description: The tracking hostname, a subdomain of the domain.

status.description: `pending` until the CNAME points at coss.com and its certificate is issued, `active` once links and open pixels of emails sent from the domain use it, `temporary_failure` when an active hostname stopped working (emails fall back to the default tracking host meanwhile), `failed` when setup gave up (72 hours) — restart it with the domain's verify endpoint. `deleting` is a removal in progress.

name.description: The fully qualified record name to create.

value.description: The host the record must point at.

status.description: What the last DNS check saw. `not_checked` means DNS has not been consulted yet.

found.description: What DNS returned when it did not match.

record.description: The DNS record to publish, with the result of the last check.

message.description: What is holding the hostname up, when the certificate provider said.

TrackingDomain.description: A domain's custom tracking domain: open pixels and click redirects of emails sent from the domain use it while it is `active`.

hostname.description: The hostname that receives email: the domain itself or a subdomain of it.

environment_id.description: The environment its received emails are delivered to.

name.description: The fully qualified record name to create.

value.description: The mail exchange the record must point at.

status.description: What the last DNS check saw: `verified` once the most preferred MX records point at coss.com. `not_checked` means DNS has not been consulted yet.

found.description: What DNS returned when it did not match.

record.description: The MX record to publish, with the result of the last check. Mail for the hostname is received as soon as it reaches coss.com; the check only shows what DNS serves.

ReceivingDomain.description: A domain's receiving hostname: email sent to any address at it becomes a received email of its environment.

status.description: `configured` when the BIMI record is valid and DMARC is enforced, `invalid` when a record exists but something is wrong (see `issues`), `missing` when there is no record, and `not_checked` until DNS has been consulted. coss.com checks DNS only: mailbox providers still validate the logo and the certificate.

name.description: Where the BIMI record was found, or looked up when there is none: `default._bimi.<domain>`, or the organizational domain's when only it has one.

certificate_url.description: The record's VMC or CMC certificate URL (`a=`).

dmarc_policy.description: The DMARC policy that applies to the domain (the organizational domain's `sp` when it has no record of its own), `null` without a DMARC record.

issues.description: What keeps the domain's logo from showing, as far as DNS tells.

DomainBimi.description: The result of the last BIMI check: whether mailbox providers can find the domain's brand logo and certificate. The record and the certificate are your own.

name.description: The domain to send from, without a scheme or path. Subdomains are allowed; internationalized domains must be punycode-encoded.

hostname.description: A subdomain of the domain to serve tracking links from, without a scheme or path. Point it at coss.com with the CNAME record the response lists.

The domain itself or a subdomain of it, without a scheme or path. Point its MX at coss.com with the record the response lists. Using the domain itself moves all of its mail to coss.com, so a subdomain is usually the better choice.

report_address.description: Where the domain's DMARC aggregate reports go (`rua=mailto:…`). `null` when this deployment doesn't receive email.

policy.description: The policy receivers apply: the record's `p` (`none` when it has none), or for a subdomain without a record of its own, its organizational domain's `sp` (else `p`).

inherited_from.description: The organizational domain whose DMARC record applies, when this domain publishes none of its own.

policy_since.description: When a DNS check first saw the current policy.

stage.description: Where the domain is on the path to enforcement: `not_checked` (DNS not checked yet), `no_record`, `monitoring` (`p=none`), `quarantine` or `reject`.

partial.description: The policy applies only partly (`pct` below 100, or `t=y`).

reporting.description: The published record sends aggregate reports to `report_address`.

ready.description: Whether `next` is safe to publish now.

record.description: The TXT record to publish at `_dmarc.<domain>`.

next.description: The next step: `publish` a first record, `add_reporting` (send reports to coss.com), `complete_rollout` (drop `pct`/`t=y`) or `tighten` to the next policy. `null` at `p=reject`.

checks.description: The readiness checks gating `next`, from the last 14 days of reports.

sources.description: The 50 sources with the most messages in the period.

checks.message: 100% of mail sent through coss.com passes DMARC (99% needed).

pct.description: Removed by RFC 9989 but still honored by many receivers.

DmarcPublishedRecord.description: The DMARC record found at `_dmarc.<domain>` by the latest DNS check.

header_from.description: The domain in the messages' From header.

via_coss.description: Signed with the domain's coss.com DKIM keys or sent from its coss.com MAIL FROM domain.

report_id.description: The reporter's own id of the report.

policy_published.description: The policy the reporter found when it evaluated the mail.

truncated.description: The report listed more rows than are kept (10,000); totals cover the kept rows.

report_id.description: The reporter's own id of the report.

policy_published.description: The policy the reporter found when it evaluated the mail.

truncated.description: The report listed more rows than are kept (10,000); totals cover the kept rows.

disposition.description: What the receiver did with the messages.

status.description: `not_enabled` without the Dedicated IPs add-on. `provisioning` while the pool is set up (`waiting` when none is free yet), then `warming`: live emails go through the pool while it warms up its IPs, sending what they can't take yet from shared IPs. `ready` once at least 95% of the last 7 days' deliveries (at least 1,000) left from your dedicated IPs. `releasing` after the add-on ends: emails are back on shared IPs, and the pool is released a day later.

ip.description: An IPv4 address of the pool.

delivered_7d.description: Deliveries from it in the last 7 days.

ips.description: The pool's IPs; the provider adds and removes them with volume.

dedicated_share.description: Share (0–1) of the last 7 days' deliveries that left from the pool's IPs (`null`: fewer than 1,000).

message.description: What is holding the pool up, if anything.

DedicatedIpPool.description: Your organization's dedicated IPs (the Dedicated IPs add-on): a pool managed and warmed up automatically.

event_types.description: Event types delivered to this endpoint. An empty array means every event type, including ones added later.

api_version.description: The API version (`Coss-Version`) events are rendered in for this endpoint. Each event carries it as `api_version`.

enabled.description: A disabled endpoint receives nothing until it is enabled again.

disabled_reason.description: `manual`: someone disabled it. `failing`: its deliveries failed every attempt for five days, so coss.com disabled it. `null` while enabled.

failing_since.description: When the endpoint's current run of failed deliveries began (a delivery that failed every attempt); cleared by the next successful delivery. An endpoint failing for five days is disabled. `null` while healthy.

previous_secret_expires_at.description: After a secret roll, deliveries are also signed with the previous secret until this time. `null` when only the current secret signs.

secret.description: The endpoint's `whsec_…` signing secret, used to verify the requests coss.com sends. Returned only when the endpoint is created and when its secret is rolled — store it now; it cannot be read back through the API.

url.description: An `https://` URL coss.com posts events to.

description.description: A note for your own reference. `null` clears it.

event_types.description: Event types delivered to this endpoint. An empty array means every event type, including ones added later. Defaults to every event type.

api_version.description: The API version (`Coss-Version`) events are rendered in for this endpoint. Each event carries it as `api_version`. Defaults to the version of the request that creates the endpoint.

event_types.description: Event types delivered to this endpoint. An empty array means every event type, including ones added later.

api_version.description: The API version (`Coss-Version`) events are rendered in for this endpoint. Each event carries it as `api_version`.

enabled.description: A disabled endpoint receives nothing until it is enabled again.

disabled_reason.description: `manual`: someone disabled it. `failing`: its deliveries failed every attempt for five days, so coss.com disabled it. `null` while enabled.

failing_since.description: When the endpoint's current run of failed deliveries began (a delivery that failed every attempt); cleared by the next successful delivery. An endpoint failing for five days is disabled. `null` while healthy.

previous_secret_expires_at.description: After a secret roll, deliveries are also signed with the previous secret until this time. `null` when only the current secret signs.

url.description: An `https://` URL coss.com posts events to.

description.description: A note for your own reference. `null` clears it.

event_types.description: Event types delivered to this endpoint. An empty array means every event type, including ones added later.

api_version.description: The API version (`Coss-Version`) events are rendered in for this endpoint. Each event carries it as `api_version`.

previous_secret_expires_in.description: Seconds the current secret keeps signing deliveries next to the new one, so receivers can switch without rejecting anything. Default 86400 (a day), at most 604800 (a week). `0` stops it immediately, e.g. after a leak.

requeued.description: How many failed deliveries were queued for one more attempt. Their attempts are spread over the next minute.

has_more.description: At most 1,000 are requeued per call; `true` means call again with the same `since`.

since.description: Requeue the endpoint's deliveries that failed and were created at or after this time (ISO 8601). Deliveries are kept for 30 days.

event_id.description: The event's id: the `id` of the payload and the `webhook-id` header.

next_attempt_at.description: When the next attempt is due; `null` once the delivery is finished.

payload.description: The event body, exactly as posted to the endpoint.

attempts.description: Every HTTP attempt of this delivery, oldest first.

WebhookDeliveryStatus.description: `pending`: waiting for its next attempt. `succeeded`: the endpoint answered with a 2xx status. `failed`: every attempt failed, or the endpoint was disabled.

status_code.description: The endpoint's HTTP status; `null` when no response arrived.

error.description: Why the attempt failed (e.g. `HTTP 500`, a timeout); `null` on success.

response_excerpt.description: At most 1 KB of the response body, as text.

api_version.description: The API version (`Coss-Version`) the listener's events are rendered in.

event_types.description: Event types the listener receives. An empty array means every event type.

expires_at.description: When the listener closes unless it is polled again; every poll moves it 10 minutes ahead.

event_types.description: Event types to receive. Defaults to every event type.

api_version.description: The API version events are rendered in. Defaults to the version of the request that creates the listener.

description.description: Where the events go, for your own reference (shown in the log).

deliveries.description: Events to forward, oldest first. Empty when none arrived while the poll waited. A delivery not acknowledged within two minutes is handed out again.

acknowledged.description: How many of the request's acknowledgements were recorded.

ack_token.description: Send it back with the delivery's acknowledgement in a later poll.

event_id.description: The event's id: the `id` of the body, and the `webhook-id` header endpoints receive.

attempt.description: How many polls have handed it out: more than 1 when an earlier answer was never acknowledged.

body.description: The event body, exactly as an endpoint with the listener's API version would receive it.

acks.description: What happened to deliveries handed out earlier. A delivery is finished once acknowledged: a 2xx status (or none, with no error) succeeds; anything else fails. Neither is retried.

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for deliveries when none is pending, in milliseconds. Default 20000, at most 25000.

limit.description: The most deliveries to hand out. Default 10, at most 50.

status_code.description: What the local URL answered; `null` when nothing answered, or when the event was only printed.

error.description: Why forwarding failed (e.g. `connection refused`); `null` if it didn't.

event.description: The event, as an endpoint on the request's API version receives it. Its `webhook-id` header is `event.id`.

endpoints.description: Enabled endpoints of the environment subscribed to the type, each sent it once.

listeners.description: Open `coss listen` listeners subscribed to the type, each handed it once.

reason.description: `bounce`: added after a permanent bounce. `complaint`: added after a spam complaint. `manual`: added one by one through the API or dashboard. `import`: added by a bulk import. `unsubscribe`: added by the recipient's one-click unsubscribe, scoped to the email's category.

suppression.description: Only for `email.suppressed`: the entry that matched the recipient.

unsubscribe.description: Only for `email.suppressed` without `suppression`: the recipient is a contact who unsubscribed (from marketing, or from the email's topic, `topic`).

url.description: The original link that was clicked.

link_position.description: Index of the link among the email's tracked links.

id.description: The event id, and the `webhook-id` header.

api_version.description: The API version (`Coss-Version`) this event is rendered in: the receiving endpoint's `api_version`.

dmarc_policy.description: The sender domain's DMARC policy (`none`, `quarantine` or `reject`) when DMARC failed.

ReceivedEmailVerdicts.description: What the receiving server concluded: `pass`, `fail`, `gray` (could not decide) or `processing_failed`; `null` when the check did not run.

id.description: The event id, also sent as the `webhook-id` header.

api_version.description: The API version (`Coss-Version`) this event is rendered in: the receiving endpoint's `api_version`.

id.description: The event id, also sent as the `webhook-id` header.

api_version.description: The API version (`Coss-Version`) this event is rendered in: the receiving endpoint's `api_version`.

outcome.description: `risk.assessment.reviewed`: the outcome that resolved the review.

RiskEvent.description: What is being assessed. `custom` events are named by `event_name`; velocity is counted per event.

RiskDecision.description: `allow`: go ahead. `review`: suspicious; let it through with limits, or hold it for a person. `block`: refuse it.

value.description: The count behind a `velocity.*` reason, or the score behind a `content.*` one.

threshold.description: What a `velocity.*` or `content.*` reason fires at.

provider.description: `ip.hosting_provider`, `ip.vpn_network`: the network's operator; `ip.vpn`: the VPN service.

previous_user.description: `duplicate.canonical_mailbox`, `duplicate.device`: your id of the user who has the mailbox or device, if known.

previous_assessment.description: `duplicate.canonical_mailbox`, `duplicate.device`: the assessment that first saw the mailbox or device.

RiskOutcome.description: What really happened: `legitimate`, `fraud`, or `abuse` (spam, free-tier abuse and the like).

id.description: The event id, and the `webhook-id` header.

api_version.description: The API version (`Coss-Version`) this event is rendered in: the receiving endpoint's `api_version`.

post.description: Queues an email from the API key's environment and returns it with `status: "queued"`; it is handed to the delivery provider moments later. Follow it with `GET /v1/emails/{id}` or the `email.sent` / `email.failed` webhooks. Live (`coss_live_…`) keys must send from a verified domain of the organization. Sandbox (`coss_test_…`) keys accept any `from` and never deliver anything; the response has `sandbox: true`. Recipients on the environment's suppression list (for every email, or for the email's `category`) are skipped and get the status `suppressed`. With a future `scheduled_at` the email is stored with the status `scheduled` and sent at that time; the domain and the suppression list are checked again then. Attachments are base64-encoded; only metadata is kept after sending. Recipients count against the organization's send quota (per second and per day; sandbox environments have their own daily quota). With open or click tracking on (the environment's settings, or `tracking`), the HTML body is delivered with a tracking pixel and/or links rewritten to coss.com redirects; the stored `html` stays as sent.

post.description: Queues up to 100 emails in one request. Each email is handled exactly as by `POST /v1/emails` (sender checks, suppressions, scheduling, attachments, tracking), but the batch is all or nothing: if any email is invalid, or any `from` is not a verified domain (live keys), nothing is stored and the error names the email (e.g. `emails.3.to`). One `Idempotency-Key` covers the whole batch. The emails' recipients are charged against the send quota together, so a batch with more recipients than the quota allows at once is refused (`quota_exceeded` without `Retry-After`): split it. The request body shares the 40 MB limit of a single send.

post.description: Replaces the endpoint's signing secret with a new one, returned in the response (the only time it is). post.description: Queues a text message from the API key's environment and returns it with `status: "queued"`; it is handed to the carrier moments later. Follow it with `GET /v1/sms/{id}` or the `sms.sent`, `sms.delivered`, `sms.undelivered` and `sms.failed` webhooks. Live (`coss_live_…`) keys send `from` one of the organization's numbers whose carrier registration is approved, to the countries the organization allows (US and Canada unless changed in the dashboard). Sandbox (`coss_test_…`) keys accept any `from`, deliver nothing and answer the SMS simulator's numbers (`+15005550006` delivered, `+15005550001` invalid, `+15005550004` filtered by the carrier, `+15005550009` opted out, `+15005550008` replies). A number on the environment's SMS suppression list (it replied STOP, or it can't receive SMS) is skipped: the message is `failed` with `suppressed`. Segments count against the organization's send quota, and each is billed by the destination country.

Sandbox (`coss_test_…`) keys accept documented test addresses (`192.0.2.x`, `@disposable.test`, `@undeliverable.test`).

post.description: Takes `cost` tokens (default 1) from `key`'s share of one of your buckets and says whether to let the request through: a 200 either way, with `allowed`. Denied requests take nothing. Each key has its own bucket of `burst` tokens refilling at `limit` per `period_seconds` (GCRA, the algorithm coss.com limits its own API with). coss.com keeps only a keyed hash of `key`. While coss.com can't count, the bucket's `on_failure` answers and `degraded` is true.
